method: Independent source and inventory review only; no browser, extension, build, permission, database, or runtime execution.

verdict_A_spec_and_procedure.overall: PARTIAL; do not populate all five inventory cases from this proposal unchanged

EXT-F-4100-T01.accepted: Admin applicability, manual runner route, repeat attach and invalid integer target are source consistent.
EXT-F-4100-T01.correction: Step 1 must list attachments before the first attach. As written it attaches first and calls that later list the baseline, then instructs the operator to stop if the owned ID appears. A successful attach necessarily adds that ID, so the procedure stops before its main assertion. Capture the list before attach, require exactly one newly present ID after successful attach, and verify the browser still focuses the owned tab before treating that ID as owned. Preserve prior list entries. After invalid target, compare the list again to ensure it did not change.

EXT-F-4101-T01.accepted: The valid owned attachment/detach cycle and avoiding an invalid target are sound; a failed detach schedules an idle timer.
EXT-F-4101-T01.correction: Take an attached-tabs baseline before attach and require exactly one new ID afterward, associated with the focused owned tab, before using the ID in detach. The proposal currently calls an ID 'newly attached' without a baseline. The inventory also has an invalid-input dimension: add a schema-negative tab_id string or other invalid schema value that the runner rejects before the handler, while keeping the unsafe invalid-target detach excluded and explaining that distinction. Verify no list change after schema rejection.

EXT-F-4102-T01.accepted: The list's in-memory scope and before/after attach/detach checks are correctly limited.
EXT-F-4102-T01.correction: The initial step cannot know the owned tab ID from attached_tabs before attach under the shared setup. Record baseline, attach the focused owned tab, require exactly one newly added ID and no concurrent attachment activity, then use that ID only. Add a schema-negative non-object argument for this no-args handler to cover the inventory's invalid-input dimension and verify it does not mutate the list. No debugger permission denial is established by this manual path.

EXT-F-4104-T01.accepted: Member and admin applicability, positive public-page read, node limit, schema-negative max_nodes, invalid target, and retained attachment follow the source.
EXT-F-4104-T01.correction: Do not require every returned node object to visibly contain all seven named keys: role, name, value, description, properties, and child_ids are read from optional Chrome AX fields and undefined properties disappear when ToolsView JSON-stringifies output. Assert stable outer shape and inspect only fields present. Take a list baseline before the first positive call and identify exactly one newly attached ID before cleanup; repeat exact-ID cleanup after the post-reload positive call in each role. State that member access through this manual runner proves handler reachability only, since cdp_attached_tabs and cdp_detach carry admin_only metadata that the runner does not enforce.

EXT-F-4112-T01.accepted: Member and admin applicability, variable metric names/values, schema-negative string, invalid target, and retained attachment follow the source.
EXT-F-4112-T01.correction: Take an attached-tabs baseline before the positive call and require exactly one new ID tied to the focused owned tab before exact-ID cleanup. The present instruction 'if the owned target appears' has no way to distinguish that target from pre-existing listed IDs. Make the same cleanup explicit after the post-reload positive call in both roles. State that member use of admin_only cleanup/list handlers through ToolsView is a manual-runner bypass and proves no dispatcher access outcome.

accepted: The proposal labels every case runtime unverified and does not claim a browser result or change inventory status.
It preserves the existing mode sets: admin only for attach/detach/list, member plus admin for accessibility and metrics; it makes no new guest applicability ruling.
It correctly scopes the manual Tools runner to direct handler behavior and disclaims dispatcher admin, Ask/Act, permission, and agent-routing conclusions.
It uses a public owned target, refuses unknown debugger ownership, avoids invalid detach targets, and names exact-ID cleanup.
corrections: Ownership cannot be inferred from an unqualified list entry. Require a pre-operation list and unique post-operation delta before any explicit-ID detach; otherwise stop without detaching unknown IDs.

The shared build receipt description omits some fields the PLAN requires: backend identity, fixture IDs, login method, principal provenance, real data origin, env flags, interception, mocks, and seeded browser state. Refer unambiguously to the full PLAN receipt or include these fields before future execution.

Do not treat pre-granted debugger permission or a manual-runner result as proof of permission enforcement. Keep the permission-denied inventory dimension unresolved or design a separately authorized dispatcher-path procedure later.
Member cleanup through admin_only handlers is a manual runner diagnostic, not proof of ordinary-member access to those handlers through dispatch.

next_action: Correct the proposal, then separately execute and record each applicable role and lifecycle pass under the existing resource/build gate. This source review does not certify dispatcher gates, permission denial, or live behavior.
